overview.headline: Weight as gravitational force and mass times acceleration

keyPoints.point: Weight is the gravitational attraction force by Earth on any object.
keyPoints.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyPoints.point: Gravity acts as a field force without contact while aerodynamic forces need contact.
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyPoints.point: Weight equals mass times gravitational acceleration described by weight equation.
keyPoints.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.

keyPoints.point: An airplane at 35000 feet weighs fewer pounds than on the surface of the earth.
keyPoints.quote: If the airplane weighs 10000 pounds on the surface of the earth, it weighs 9965 pounds at 35000 feet
